title: parse() collapses comma-separated arrays into a string when interpretNumericEntities is used with iso-8859-1
property: with comma:true, 'a=b,c' parses to {a:['b','c']} regardless of whether interpretNumericEntities/charset are also set (the entity pass only rewrites values, it must not change their shape)
input: parse('a=b,c', { comma: true, charset: 'iso-8859-1', interpretNumericEntities: true })
evidence: parseValues splits the value into an array via parseArrayValue (comma:true), then `val = interpretNumericEntities(String(val))` at lib/parse.js:191 stringifies the array with Array#toString, rejoining it with ',' and returning a string. The README documents comma:true as parsing comma-separated values into arrays; without interpretNumericEntities the same input yields ['b','c'].
